English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Alteration of papa.[1]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpɒpə/
  • Audio (Midwestern US):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɒpə

Noun

[edit]

poppa (plural poppas)

  1. (US, colloquial, sometimes childish) father, papa.

References

[edit]
  1. ^ “poppa”, in Lexico, Dictionary.com; Oxford University Press, 2019–2022.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • PPPoA

Finnish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpopːɑ/, [ˈpo̞pːɑ̝]
  • Rhymes: -opːɑ
  • Syllabification(key): pop‧pa
  • Hyphenation(key): pop‧pa

Etymology 1

[edit]

Child speak, possibly based on polttaa.

Adjective

[edit]

poppa (comparative popempi, superlative popin) (childish)

  1. hot

Icelandic

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

(This etymology is missing or incomplete. Please add to it, or discuss it at the Etymology scriptorium.)

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpʰɔhpa/
  • Rhymes: -ɔhpa

Verb

[edit]

poppa (weak verb, third-person singular past indicative poppaði, supine poppað)

  1. (intransitive) to make popcorn
    Eigum við að poppa?
    Should we make popcorn?
  2. to pop popcorn or the maize kernel [with accusative]
    • Icelandic Web of Science: Er virkilega hægt að poppa maísbaun með því að láta farsíma hringja umhverfis baunina, eins og sýnt er á myndböndum á Netinu? (“Can you really pop a maize kernel by surrounding it with ringing mobiles like shown on Internet videos?”)
      Er virkilega hægt að poppa maísbaun með því að láta farsíma hringja umhverfis baunina, eins og sýnt er á myndböndum á Netinu?
      Can you really pop a maize kernel by surrounding it with ringing mobiles like shown on Internet videos?

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpop.pa/
  • Rhymes: -oppa
  • Hyphenation: póp‧pa

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Vulgar Latin puppa (“breast, teat, nipple, boob”), from Latin puppa, variant of pupa (“girl; doll”). Doublet of pupa.

Noun

[edit]

poppa f (plural poppe)

  1. (informal) breast, boob
    Synonyms: poccia, tetta
Related terms
[edit]
  • poppare

Etymology 2

[edit]

From Latin puppis, through a Vulgar Latin *puppa.

Noun

[edit]

poppa f (plural poppe)

  1. (nautical) stern
    Antonym: prua
Descendants
[edit]
  • → Maltese: poppa
  • → Turkish: pupa

Etymology 3

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

poppa

  1. inflection of poppare:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Anagrams

[edit]
  • pappo, pappò

Maltese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian poppa.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpɔp.pa/
  • Rhymes: -ɔppa

Noun

[edit]

poppa f (plural poppi)

  1. (nautical) stern, poop

Derived terms

[edit]
  • qasru tal-poppa

Swedish

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

poppa (present poppar, preterite poppade, supine poppat, imperative poppa)

  1. to pop (popcorn)
    Vi poppade popcorn
    We popped / made popcorn
